name: minidjvu
desc: DjVu multipage encoder, single page encoder/decoder
why: A DjVu encoder and decoder opens up the odd, long-forgotten DjVu scanned-document format, a decent file-format poke.

brief.what_it_is: minidjvu is a command-line utility that encodes and decodes single-page black-and-white DjVu files, and can also compress multiple pages together by exploiting similarities between them. It takes bitmap input in PBM, Windows BMP, or TIFF (via libtiff) and produces DjVu files. The Windows build includes a minimal GUI, which is a JavaScript-based web page that can run as an application under Internet Explorer.
brief.why_it_exists: The author describes it as an experiment: it takes the black-and-white part of DjVu, called JB2, and works with that on its own. The README says it is not meant to support all of DjVu.
brief.how_it_works: minidjvu is built on DjVuLibre, the primary DjVu support library. It handles only the bitonal JB2 layer, and the README does not describe the internal encoding steps. For multipage mode, the README says that pages are named after their source images with the extension changed to djvu, with a numerical suffix added on a name clash. Pages can be bundled or indirect.
brief.install_notes: The README says the Linux source tarball requires the libtiff development package. A Windows installable package is provided. The homepage text does not mention brew, and I did not check the Project Page for build or configuration steps. Localization uses gettext, which the README says does not work under Windows.
brief.standout: It was built as a deliberately narrow experiment: a bitonal-only DjVu encoder that exploits shared glyphs across pages. The README says the 0.8 pattern-matching changes were made to stop unrelated shapes from being merged, which is a fairly concrete, odd detail about how JB2 symbol matching can go wrong.
brief.status: Latest version is 0.8, and the README says it is the latest release. No release date or last-commit date appears on the homepage, so recency cannot be confirmed. The README reads as a finished release announcement, not as active development. Status: unknown, with a lean toward quiet.
brief.caveats: Only black-and-white (bitonal) content is supported; the README says it does not implement all of DjVu. Input is limited to PBM, BMP, and TIFF. The gettext localization does not work on Windows. The Windows GUI is a web page that runs under Internet Explorer. The README says the 0.8 release changed multipage naming, and the old 'pattern' parameter was removed. I did not check the license.
quotes: minidjvu is a command line utility which encodes and decodes single page black-and-white DjVu files, and can compress multiple pages, taking advantage from similarities between pages.
Minidjvu is not going to support all DjVu functionality; the idea is rather to take the black-and-white part (also called JB2) and experiment with it.
bugfix: specifying aggression level above 100 actually resulted in producing larger files.
fetch_log: https://minidjvu.sourceforge.net/ : fetched OK. Homepage text includes the README-style description, the 0.8 release notes, and the author credits. It did not include any command lines. The 'Project Page' link was not followed.

judge.reason: A narrow encoder that exposes JB2’s cross-page glyph sharing—and its failure modes—offers a genuinely odd compression idea beyond merely converting document formats.

entry.title: minidjvu
entry.tldr: A small encoder and decoder for the black-and-white layer of DjVu, which squeezes scanned pages by reusing shared letter shapes across a whole document.
entry.deeper_look:
minidjvu turns bitmaps (PBM, BMP or TIFF) into DjVu files and back again. It handles only the bitonal layer of DjVu, called JB2, and ignores the colour and photo parts of the format. It sits on top of DjVuLibre, the main DjVu support library.

Its interesting trick is multipage mode. Scanned text repeats the same shapes over and over: every lowercase e on a page looks much like every other e. The README says minidjvu compresses multiple pages together, "taking advantage from similarities between pages". Pages can be bundled into one file or kept as indirect files, named after their source images with a numeric suffix added on a name clash.

The author calls it an experiment: "Minidjvu is not going to support all DjVu functionality; the idea is rather to take the black-and-white part (also called JB2) and experiment with it." The 0.8 notes show where this gets tricky. The pattern-matching changes were made to stop unrelated shapes from being merged. That failure mode is a good way into how symbol-matching compression works, and what goes wrong when it matches too eagerly.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the usage text and the list of options, including the encoding controls, so you can see what the tool exposes.

entry.whats_unique: It is a deliberately narrow tool: just the JB2 layer of DjVu, built as a playground for cross-page symbol sharing rather than as a full DjVu toolkit.
entry.caveats: Only black-and-white content is supported, input is limited to PBM, BMP and TIFF, and the project looks quiet, with 0.8 as the latest release and no date given on the homepage.
